title: Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Akiva
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, end of chapter 6: an incident in which Rabbi Akiva made a feast for his son Shimon, and over each jug he said, “Good wine,” etc. The incident is cited in Shabbat 67a, but his son’s name is not mentioned there.

His precious son died in his lifetime, in Semachot, chapter 8: when Rabbi Shimon, Rabbi Akiva’s son, was ill, Rabbi Akiva did not suspend his academy’s teaching; and when Shimon died, his father eulogized him and said: “I know that he is destined for the world to come, for he brought merit to the many.”

notes.text: The supplied Shabbat 67a is retained alongside saved Davidson 67b, whose son is unnamed and whose vessels are cups rather than Hyman’s jugs. Saved Vilna digital Tractate Semachot 8:13 makes Rabbi Akiva the teacher who continued teaching while his son Shimon was ill; the English now states that subject explicitly.
